STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
restart:

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
We load our package:

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
with(IntegrableConnections);

STYLE='2D Output' PROMPT=''


STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
The library linalg is also needed.

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
with(linalg):

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
We load OreModules in order to use the procedure to write a D-finite partial differential system to an integrable connection.

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
with(OreModules):

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
BrycLetac system in dimension 2 - Gaussian Case

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
We define the OreAlgebra (needed for OreModules):

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
Alg2:=DefineOreAlgebra(diff=[d1,x1],diff=[d2,x2],polynom=[x1,x2],comm=[d,a]):

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
We give the equations of the system:

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
R2 := matrix(2,1,[-(1/2)*d*d2+d1^2-x2*d2^2,2*d1*d2+x1*d2^2]);

STYLE='2D Output' PROMPT=''
PTYiNiQ7IiIiIiIjO0YmRiZFXFtsIzYkRiZGJiwoKiZJImRHRiNGJkkjZDJHRiNGJiMhIiJGJyokSSNkMUdGI0YnRiYqJkkjeDJHRiNGJkYuRidGMDYkRidGJiwmKiZGLkYnSSN4MUdGI0YmRiYqJkYyRiZGLkYmRic=

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
We write the system as an integrable connection:

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
C2:=OreModules[Connection](R2,Alg2);

STYLE='2D Output' PROMPT=''


STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
If we want to know the basis of the associated module in which the connection is written, we can use the procedure KBasis of OreModules:

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
OreModules[KBasis](R2,Alg2);

STYLE='2D Output' PROMPT=''
NyYmSSdsYW1iZGFHNiI2IyIiIiomSSNkMkdGJUYnRiNGJyomSSNkMUdGJUYnRiNGJyomRikiIiNGI0Yn

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
We define the right-hand sides of the connection.

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
b1:=vector(4,[0,0,1,0]);
b2:=vector(4,[0,0,0,0]);

STYLE='2D Output' PROMPT=''
PTYiNiM7IiIiIiIlRVxbbCVGJiIiISIiI0YpIiIkRiZGJ0Yp

STYLE='2D Output' PROMPT=''
PTYiNiM7IiIiIiIlRVxbbCVGJiIiISIiI0YpIiIkRilGJ0Yp

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
We use our procedures for computing rational solutions of the integrable connection. The right-hand sides are given as last input.

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
RationalSolutions(C2,[x1,x2],['param',[d],'rhs',[b1,b2]]);

STYLE='2D Output' PROMPT=''
NyQ9NiI2JDsiIiIiIiU7RiciIiRFXFtsLTYkRipGJyomSSJkR0YkRidJI3gxR0YkRic2JEYoRioiIiE2JEYnRicsJiomRi8iIiNGLkYnI0YnRjVJI3gyR0YkRjU2JEY1RjVGMTYkRipGNUYnNiRGKEY1RjE2JEY1RidGNTYkRjVGKkYxNiRGKEYnRjE2JEYnRipGJzYkRipGKkYxNiRGJ0Y1Ri89RiQ2JEYmO0YnRidFXFtsJUYsRi9GMiwkKiRGL0Y1RjZGO0YxRj1GMQ==

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
The ouput contains a matrix whose columns form a basis of rational solutions of the homogeneous integrable connection and a vector that is a particular 
solution of the non-homogeneous integrable connection. A solution is then given by the sum of a linear combination of the columns of the matrix and the vector.

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
BrycLetac system in dimension 3 - Gaussian Case

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
We define the OreAlgebra (needed for OreModules):

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
Alg3:=DefineOreAlgebra(diff=[d1,x1],diff=[d2,x2],diff=[d3,x3],polynom=[x1,x2,x3],comm=[d]):

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
We give the equations of the system:

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
R3 := matrix(3,1,[-d*d2+d1^2-x2*d2^2-2*x3*d2*d3,-(1/2)*d*d3+2*d1*d2+x1*d2^2-x3*d3^2,2*d1*d3+d2^2+2*x1*d2*d3+x2*d3^2]);

STYLE='2D Output' PROMPT=''


STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
We write the system as an integrable connection:

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
C3:=OreModules[Connection](R3,Alg3):

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
If we want to know the basis of the associated module in which the connection is written, we can use the procedure KBasis of OreModules:

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
OreModules[KBasis](R3,Alg3);

STYLE='2D Output' PROMPT=''
NyomSSdsYW1iZGFHNiI2IyIiIiomSSNkM0dGJUYnRiNGJyomRiNGJ0kjZDJHRiVGJyomSSNkMUdGJUYnRiNGJyomRikiIiNGI0YnKihGK0YnRilGJ0YjRicqKEYtRidGKUYnRiNGJyomRikiIiRGI0Yn

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
We define the right-hand sides:

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
b1:=vector(8,[0$3,1,0$4]);
b2:=vector(8,[0$8]);
b3:=eval(b2);

STYLE='2D Output' PROMPT=''
PTYiNiM7IiIiIiIpRVxbbClGJiIiISIiI0YpIiIkRikiIiVGJiIiJkYpIiInRikiIihGKUYnRik=

STYLE='2D Output' PROMPT=''
PTYiNiM7IiIiIiIpRVxbbClGJiIiISIiI0YpIiIkRikiIiVGKSIiJkYpIiInRikiIihGKUYnRik=

STYLE='2D Output' PROMPT=''
PTYiNiM7IiIiIiIpRVxbbClGJiIiISIiI0YpIiIkRikiIiVGKSIiJkYpIiInRikiIihGKUYnRik=

STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
We use our procedure for computing rational solutions of the integrable connection:

STYLE='Maple Input' PROMPT='> '
RationalSolutions(C3,[x1,x2,x3],['rhs',[b1,b2,b3],'param',[d]]);

STYLE='2D Output' PROMPT=''


STYLE='Text' PROMPT=''
The ouput contains a matrix whose columns form a basis of rational solutions of the homogeneous integrable connection and a vector that is a particular 
solution of the non-homogeneous integrable connection. A solution is then given by the sum of a linear combination of the columns of the matrix and the vector.
